title: Shortest Path in a Weighted Tree
summary: Given an integer n and a weighted tree with n nodes, where edges are defined by a 2D array, you can update edge weights or compute the shortest path from the root to any node.
statement: Given an integer n and a weighted tree with n nodes, where edges are defined by a 2D array, you can update edge weights or compute the shortest path from the root to any node. For updates, a 2D array specifies new weights. For queries, a 2D array asks for the shortest path distance from node 1 to a given node. The output is an array of these distances.
constraints: edges form a weighted undirected tree rooted at node 1 with up to 100,000 nodes.
An update [1,u,v,w] changes one existing edge weight; a query [2,x] asks for the current root-to-x distance.
Return answers for distance queries in their original order.
hints: Changing a parent edge shifts the distance of every node in exactly one rooted subtree by the same delta.
Euler-tour each subtree into a contiguous interval, then use Fenwick range-add and point-query updates.
Compute parent, base distance, and entry/exit times; range-add each edge delta to its child subtree and point-query requested nodes.
Euler intervals contain exactly the descendants whose paths use the updated edge, so base distance plus accumulated deltas is current.
editorial: Euler intervals contain exactly the descendants whose paths use the updated edge, so base distance plus accumulated deltas is current.

tests.explanation: Node two is first distance seven; updating its only edge changes the next answer to four.
The root has distance zero, and updating edge 1-3 changes only node three’s distance.
